newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy commercial vehicle sales slump in September.
newsitem.headline: Italy commercial vehicle sales slump in September.

text.p: Italian commercial vehicle sales slumped 12.2 percent to 11,199 units in September over the same 1995 month, industry association data showed.
But cumulative sales in the first nine months were up 2.3 percent at 106,819 vehicles, a joint statement from makers association Anfia and importing body Unrae said.
The positive balance was mainly due to the effect of strong gains made in the first months of the year, they said.
In September, Italian manufacturers saw deliveries down 18 percent to 6,188, taking their market share to 54.6 percent from 58.47 percent.
Fiat Auto sales fell 5.8 percent to 4,332 and Iveco plunged 47.9 percent to 1,268, but Piaggio sales rose 24.9 percent to 476.

Among the main foreign marques imported, Ford saw sales fall 20.6 percent in September to 1,303 and Renault dropped 30.9 percent to 519. But Nissan sales rose 3.8 percent to 882, Mercedes rose 22.5 percent to 665, Citroen rose 50.9 percent to 261 and Volkswagen jumped 89.2 percent to 420.
